title: Helium bubble replenishment keeps MSR fuel clean
summary: Researchers at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Argonne National Laboratory have developed models to predict how helium bubbles behave in the liquid fuel of molten salt reactors. Unlike conventional reactors, where fission products remain trapped in fuel pellets, fission products in an MSR circulate throughout the system and can create operational challenges if not properly managed.

title: Report looks at reasons for Vogtle construction delays
summary: A lack of a realistic schedule; a failure to adhere to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s quality assurance requirements; and changes to Westinghouse’s AP1000 incomplete reactor design during construction were the primary reasons Vogtle-3 and -4 suffered delays, a new report says. Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy (CGEP) issued its report, “Insights into Construction Delays at the Vogtle Nuclear Plant: Primary Sources of Delay Identified by the Independent Construction Monitor,” on November 15. This report investigated the delays that ultimately made the country’s most recent commercial reactor project a costly affair and outlined the lessons learned that current and future projects can take from Vogtle.

title: Type One Energy, UTK receive IRIS grant for fusion R&D
summary: The Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development (TNECD) Office of Innovation has awarded its inaugural Innovation and Research for Industry Success (IRIS) grant to stellarator fusion technology developer Type One Energy, in partnership with the University of Tennessee–Knoxville. Type One Energy, which is headquartered in Knoxville, is working with UTK on a two-year project to develop a new class of coated ceramic breeder particles to be used in the production and management of tritium fuel for future fusion power plants.

title: Framatome Inaugurates Major Components Facility As France Prepares For Reactor Rollout
summary: Framatome, the nuclear engineering subsidiary of French state-owned utility EDF, has inaugurated a new €100m ($109m) nuclear component manufacturing facility as France prepares to advance its next generation of nuclear power projects. The facility at Le Creusot in eastern France is dedicated to the manufacturing and assembly of nuclear reactor pressure vessel internals. Framatome said the project entailed the acquisition and complete transformation of roughly 15,000 m2 of industrial spaces, with the integration of large-scale machining, welding and assembly equipment.

title: Pacific Fusion Gets Key Licence For $1 Billion New Mexico Demonstration Facility
summary: US-based Pacific Fusion announced that the New Mexico Environment Department (NMED) has approved its radioactive materials licence, enabling the company to operate a fusion machine and accelerate its efforts to bring fusion energy to the grid. The licence authorises Pacific Fusion to possess and use tritium for fusion at its $1bn (€910m) research and manufacturing campus in Albuquerque, a facility that will house its demonstration fusion system. The company said this is the first radioactive materials licence New Mexico has ever issued to a private fusion company, and enables key research supporting the company’s goal of net facility gain by 2030, generating more energy output than the energy used to power the system.
